candidate: Fault blade V11 final focused pair
scope: Independent actual-pixel comparison with original053 and frozen V10. Only final front/profile diagnostic views; no full render set or engine revalidation.
improvements: Profile exposes actual layered stone depth rather than a thick monolithic shell.
Brown grip is closer in hue to the source than V10 gray.
The straight V10 crystal opening has a more varied boundary.

remaining.finding: Broad near-planar flagstone cells still dominate. The upper row reads as regularly adjacent plates; profile reads as a few long parallel layers. The source has more overlapping chipped lips, uneven thickness and interleaved mineral scales around the crystal.
remaining.nextRepair: Fit a smaller number of source-recognizable overlapping plate clusters with broken bevel lips, varied longitudinal depth and exposed undercuts; judge front and profile together rather than filling the blade with regular tiles.

remaining.finding: Final front crystal reads as a narrow zigzag purple channel with a mostly continuous opening; source has wider irregular faceted exposures and distinct crystal volumes that interact with overlapping stone.
remaining.nextRepair: Use several irregular exposure windows and faceted crystal volumes, preserving real containment in profile; avoid another uniform inset stripe.

remaining.finding: Guard remains a simple open cylindrical bronze collar with repeated flanges, lacking the source layered studs and stone-bearing ornament. Pommel shows one large purple prism within a few brown shell faces rather than a compact mixed crystal/stone cluster.
remaining.nextRepair: Rebuild the guard silhouette and pommel cluster from source component forms before additional microtexture.

remaining.finding: Grip is browner but broad flat wraps and thin dark diagonal seams remain mechanically regular. Stone remains uniformly taupe; bronze reads dark and undifferentiated.
remaining.nextRepair: Give leather actual overlapping band thickness and restrained edge variation; distinguish stone fracture faces and bronze worn edges under the same neutral light.

decision: The focused pair is useful diagnostic evidence and contains genuine depth changes, but it is not an exact-match improvement across all major forms. Keep unapproved; do not infer production acceptance or full-view completion.
limitations: Approximate camera matching and different illustrated/rendered lighting; no measured dimension assertion from these images.
No full backside, hand fit, LOD/collision, GPU/material parity or gameplay review.
